title: Landfill Manager: Carcass Truck Queue Past 12 Hours

fields.systemName: Recorded Line: EOC Operations Desk, Training Room

caller.name: Rhys Tolliver
caller.label: Landfill Manager, Calder County Regional Landfill

callee.name: Alina Petrova
callee.label: Deputy Director / Operations, Calder County EOC

transcript.speaker: OPS
transcript.text: Calder County EOC, Operations.

transcript.speaker: LANDFILL
transcript.text: It's Rhys Tolliver at the Regional Landfill on Larkin Road. I need you, the Director and the Sheriff on this. The first sealed carcass load reached my gate at 17:20 yesterday. It's 05:38 now, so that load has been waiting more than 12 hours.

transcript.speaker: OPS
transcript.text: How many are in line?

transcript.speaker: LANDFILL
transcript.text: Fourteen trucks, about 20 tons each. That's roughly 280 tons lined up on my entrance road. I can't tip a single one until MPCA signs. Their project manager says the approval letter 'should' be signed around 10:00. Should.

transcript.speaker: LANDFILL
transcript.text: And even once it's signed, this response gets 120 tons a day from me. That's more than two days just for the trucks already here, and barn 4 hasn't even loaded yet.

transcript.speaker: OPS
transcript.text: Okay. What about the drivers?

transcript.speaker: LANDFILL
transcript.text: Two of them have been in their cabs since yesterday afternoon. I can't let them get out and walk around my site, and nobody's relieved them. And one trailer, the fourth truck back, has a seep at the rear seal. There's fluid on the gravel under the back doors. I've put absorbent down, but I don't want that trailer sitting there another day.

transcript.speaker: OPS
transcript.text: Is there anywhere else they can go?

transcript.speaker: LANDFILL
transcript.text: I called the Pell County Landfill scale house. They'll start taking loads at 07:00 and they said up to 8. But they want a Board of Animal Health movement permit for every load and a set route, no stops. And they're capped at 90 tons a day, so realistically that's four of my trucks today and the rest tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: LANDFILL
transcript.text: So here's what I need. Somebody has to tell these drivers where they're going, who gives them a permit number, and which checkpoint they go out through, because the deputies will stop them without one. Pell opens in an hour and twenty minutes.

transcript.speaker: OPS
transcript.text: Understood. Stay by your phone. We'll call you back.

voiceStyles.LANDFILL: Man in his 50s, flat and tired after a night on site, clipped and practical, diesel engines idling behind him
voiceStyles.OPS: Calm EOC staffer, early-morning voice, typing between lines

instructorNote: This call trips two escalation triggers: the landfill queue is over 12 hours, and the pile is too big for one site. Watch whether the Director calls the state EOC now and whether Ops asks the Board for a carcass movement permit for each load and to have the leaking trailer fixed. Also watch whether the Sheriff names a sealed-load route out through a staffed checkpoint with cleaning and disinfection, and whether anyone arranges rest and relief for the drivers. Pell's 90-ton daily cap means only about four loads can leave today, so expect players to also look at the other disposal options.
